LLM-Review +1 on Gerrit 1704 — PASS with 4 ADVISORY (non-blocking) findings, all four already marked unresolved=false so none blocks submit. Recorded here so they are not lost:

1. (correctness, enrich_drain.py:99-111) The reclaim path holds no exclusion between stamped_file_is_stale and the os.unlink, unlike the mkdir leg, which is safe only because its caller already holds the fcntl leg. Assessment: real window, bounded harm. Two drainers can both condemn the same orphan, and the loser's unlink can remove the winner's freshly-created lock, so mutual exclusion can be defeated and two drains run concurrently. That is NOT a correctness hazard here: the docstring already states this lock only stops redundant WORK, and the queue claim is separately optimistic and lease-bounded, so a double drain costs duplicated effort, never a wrong result. It is also strictly better than the pre-fix property it replaces, which was a PERMANENT wedge. Closing the window properly means giving the drain lock a kernel leg (flock) or an atomic rename dance — a change to the locking MECHANISM, which is beyond 'add staleness and reclaim' and is exactly the kind of thing to escalate rather than smuggle into this fix.
2. (maintainability, enrich_drain.py:64-70) _describe_drain_lock_holder collapses a torn/incomplete v2 stamp into 'an unstamped drain lock', whereas doctor's _existence_report distinguishes 'unknown (incomplete ownership stamp)'. Genuine inconsistency I introduced; the two surfaces should use one vocabulary.
3. (tests, doctor_locks.py:287) The two non-empty holder_description branches on the drain row — 'unrecognised ownership stamp' and 'incomplete ownership stamp' — are untested.
4. (tests, enrich_drain.py:114) The stamp-write-failure branch (os.write raises, WARNING, still return the fd) is untested.

Items 2-4 are cheap quality work on code this change introduced; item 1 needs a design decision. Landing patch set 1 as-is rather than gambling another multi-hour CI cycle on this host's flaky runner capacity, and filing these as a follow-up ticket linked discovered_from.

CI (run 31671006152) has every non-pytest job green — lint + type-check, golden-path, artifact provenance, optionality, eval discipline, ticket resolvability, verify-identity — with the four-way pytest matrix still running. Verified has not voted yet, so the ticket stays in_progress.
